page: Hetzner Cloud cax21 is an arm64 virtual server belonging to the provider's Cost Optimized family, virtualized via QEMU. The instance provides 4 shared vCPUs backed by an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor running at 2.0 GHz with one thread per core. Memory capacity is set at 8.0 GB, yielding 1.95 GB per vCPU. Hardware resources include 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The configuration includes no dedicated graphics hardware and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results show balanced output in select multi-threaded and memory-intensive evaluations, achieving average tier results in stress-ng single-core (1777.99) and multi-core (7055.54) testing. Memory read throughput on large blocks reaches 45.11 GB/sec, while write operations reach 26.08 GB/sec. PassMark database operations also place in the average category with a score of 2684.51. However, most broader compute and compilation benchmarks place in the lower quartiles. Geekbench scores reach 1005.0 for single-core and 3335.0 for multi-core, with software compilation scoring 4748.0. Specific workloads such as CPU encryption (637.38) and image processing (1893.0) fall into the bottom decile.

Given its shared processor allocation and lack of advanced vector extensions such as AVX or AMX, the cax21 architecture prioritizes resource density and cost efficiency over high-frequency execution. With an 80 GB NVMe storage volume and a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance provides a balanced footprint for arm64 software development, staging environments, web serving, and basic database operations that do not require dedicated core capacity.
description: Hetzner Cloud cax21 is an arm64 instance type from the Cost Optimized family, providing 4 shared vCPUs on an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz alongside 8.0 GB of RAM and 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Virtualized through QEMU, the instance delivers a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio without a GPU or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Synthetic testing shows mid-tier performance in multi-core stress-ng tests and large-block memory transfers, alongside average execution in PassMark database operations. Conversely, general compute benchmarks such as Geekbench single-core, multi-core, and software compilation register in the lower performance quartiles, reflecting shared vCPU scheduling and moderate clock speeds. Cryptographic tests and image processing also exhibit lower baseline throughput. Given its resource profile, cax21 offers budget-oriented compute capacity suited for arm64 application testing, lightweight container hosting, staging environments, and basic database workloads where top-tier single-threaded compute is not required.
